newsitem.title: JAPAN: Summers calls on Japan to attain growth target-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Summers calls on Japan to attain growth target-MOF.

text.p: U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers has called on Japan to achieve its official economic growth target of 1.9 percent for 1997/98 led by domestic demand, a senior Finance Ministry official said on Tuesday.

"It is desirable for Japan to achieve real growth of 1.9 percent for the next fiscal year led by domestic demand," Summers was quoted as saying by the official, who briefed reporters on a meeting between Summers and Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka.
Summers is in Tokyo for a "Six Markets" meeting on Tuesday between finance and central bank officials of Japan, the United States, Australia, Hong Kong, Singapore and China.
In the meeting with Mitsuzuka, Summers expressed concern about a sharp rise in Japan's current account surplus, the official said.
He said Mitsuzuka and Summers did not specifically discuss foreign exchange rates.
But Mitsuzuka was quoted as saying foreign exchange rates have been stable since the meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations in February.
Mitsuzuka assured Summers that Japan's trade surplus is unlikely to increase sharply and that exports are not expected to increase substantially either, the official said.
The finance minister and Summers discussed Japan's economic and budget situations and issues regarding Japan's financial system, the official said.
Mitsuzuka assured Summers that there was no need for concern about Japan's financial system, he said.
The Finance Ministry and the Bank of Japan are taking appropriate measures to deal with any problems involving Japan's financial system, Mitsuzuka was quoted as saying.
Mitsuzuka also told Summers that Japan will make efforts to achieve growth led by domestic demand, the official said.
